proposals.program_name: MK48 MOD 7 Common Broadband Advanced Sonar System (CBASS)
proposals.announcement_evidence: engineering services in support of the Mk 48 Mod 7 Torpedo Common Broadband Advanced Sonar System (CBASS)
proposals.lexicon_quote: MK48 MOD 7 Common Broadband Advanced Sonar System (CBASS)
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the CBASS by its full Mod 7 designator, which is the same string the WPN line 3225 'MK-48 Torpedo ADCAP Mods' carries in its own narrative (only spacing in 'MK48'/'Mk 48' differs, hence designator-normalized). The award buys the engineering that develops the Mod 7 CBASS capability upgrades and weapon-component changes at NUWC Newport - i.e. the modification work the ADCAP Mods line exists to fund - rather than support for a platform that merely carries the torpedo. The competing index owner of the same name is 6120 'Spares and Repair Parts', which buys CBASS spares, not upgrade engineering, so the Mods line is the better owner.

refute_a.reason: Money colour cannot be shown to belong to BLI 3225 (account 1507N, Weapons Procurement Navy): the record names no appropriation at all, and the scope it does name is a cost-reimbursement/cost-plus-fixed-fee IDIQ for 'engineering services in support of' NUWC Newport's spiral development program - technology assessment, component design analysis, software upgrade development, critical item testing and certification - which is RDT&E-shaped development engineering, not the modification hardware a WPN ADCAP Mods procurement line buys; the lake holds no funding accounts for this PIID either, so nothing rebuts the doubt and §3's 'engineering support' pattern applies.

refute_b.reason: The CBASS name is owned by two publishable rows in this index (3225 'MK48 MOD 7 Common Broadband Advanced Sonar System (CBASS)' and 6120 'MK-48 Common Broadband Advanced Sonar System (CBASS)' - 'Spares and Repair Parts' does not match CATCHALL_TITLE, so that owner can publish), and the announcement's actual evidence - engineering services for NUWC Newport's spiral development program, technology assessment, component design analysis, software upgrade development and certification - is development work that links at least as well to RDT&E PE 0205632N 'MK-48 ADCAP', which owns 'MK-48 ADCAP', 'The Torpedo APB (TAPB)' and 'MK 48 MOD 9 ADCAP Software Testbed (AST)'; three index owners fit the same words, so the name does not identify 3225.

proposals.announcement_evidence: procurement of 14 electronic consolidated automated support system radio frequency mission equipment kits
proposals.rationale: The announcement spells out 'consolidated automated support system' and the buy is for its radio-frequency mission-equipment kits in support of PMA260, the aviation support-equipment program office; the electronic CASS is the successor variant of the AN/USM-636 CASS the APN line 0705 'Common Ground Equipment' owns, so the designator differs only by variant. The action is a procurement funded with fiscal 2025 aircraft procurement (Navy) money against a procurement line that buys exactly this test-station hardware, which is the line's own end item and not a platform it supports. The only other index owner of the CASS name is the RDT&E PE 0205633N, and this is a production buy, not development.

refute_a.reason: Money and mission both hold: the announcement obligates fiscal 2025 aircraft procurement (Navy) funds and the lake records 017-1506 (APN) on this PIID, which is exactly BLI 0705's account 1506N; the eCASS RF mission-equipment kits are the test-station hardware the Common Ground Equipment line buys as its own end item (PMA260 is the program office, not a platform the contract merely supports), and 'Common Ground Equipment' is not a CATCHALL_TITLE aggregate.

refute_b.reason: Two different index rows own a CASS name - 0705 'AN/USM-636 Consolidated Automated Support System (CASS)' and RDT&E PE 0205633N 'Consolidated Automated Support System (CASS)' (Aviation Improvements), the latter carrying the bare name the announcement's phrase actually matches - and on top of the collision the announcement buys the ELECTRONIC CASS (eCASS, AN/USM-705) RF mission-equipment kits, a different designator from both the AN/USM-636 legacy CASS and the AN/USM-702 RTCASS the proposed row owns, so this is a different variant from the one the lexicon name designates.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Aegis Platform Systems Engineering Agent (PSEA) activities and Aegis Modernization Advanced Capability Build engineering
proposals.rationale: 'Aegis Modernization' appears verbatim (case aside) in the announcement and is a name PE 0604307N 'Surface Combatant Combat System Engineering' owns in its own J-book narrative. The award incrementally funds the Aegis Platform Systems Engineering Agent and the Advanced Capability Build engineering - combat-system engineering for the CG 47 and DDG 51 classes - which is precisely the engineering work this RDT&E PE funds, not construction, not spares, and not a service the ships merely receive. The ship classes named are the recipients of the modernization, not the thing being proposed as the program.

refute_a.reason: This is the documented failure mode - O&M sustainment attached to an RDT&E line: PE 0604307N carries account 1319N (017-1319, RDT&E Navy), but the only funding accounts the lake records for N0002409C5103 are 017-1804 (O&M, Navy) and 097-0300, disjoint from the line's appropriation, and the announcement's own description of the scope it funds is the PSEA 'managing the in-service combat systems configurations', i.e. in-service sustainment; the record never names an RDT&E appropriation, so the award's money cannot be shown to belong to this PE.

refute_b.reason: 'AEGIS Modernization (AMOD)' has exactly one owner in this index (0604307N) and the announcement writes it verbatim; the only nearby competitor is 0604501N 'AEGIS Capability Build (ACB)' picking up the 'Advanced Capability Build' half of the quote, but that PE is Advanced Above Water Sensors and would not own the Aegis Platform Systems Engineering Agent's in-service configuration management and capability integration for CG 47/DDG 51, so the evidence does not link equally well elsewhere and the alias is real, not invented.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the U.S. SSGN attack weapon control system (to include training and support equipment)
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the SSGN attack weapon control system word for word, and BLI 5420 'SSN Combat Control Systems' carries both 'Attack Weapon Control System (AWCS)' and 'SSGN Attack Weapons Systems (AWS)' in its own narrative, so the owner is unambiguous inside this index. The modification is described as 'new procurement efforts' including the AWCS with its training and support equipment - procurement-appropriation work against a procurement line - so the money colour and the mission both belong to this line rather than to an O&M sustainment account. The AWCS is the program itself here, not a platform the contract supports.

refute_a.reason: Procurement work against a procurement line: the announcement calls the scope 'new procurement efforts' for the SSGN attack weapon control system with its training and support equipment, and the lake records 017-1810 (OPN) among this PIID's funding accounts, matching BLI 5420's account 1810N; the AWCS is the end item the SSN Combat Control Systems line buys, not a platform the contract merely supports, and the line is a specific combat-control-system line rather than a rollup.

refute_b.reason: 'Attack Weapon Control System (AWCS)' occurs exactly once in the index (5420), which additionally owns 'SSGN Attack Weapons Systems (AWS)' - the very SSGN qualifier the announcement uses - and the only other 'attack weapon' rows are the unrelated Compact Rapid Attack Weapon (0101226N, 2210); the name is written verbatim, no variant or increment is in dispute, and the evidence is the system name rather than the contractor's.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the missile fire control for the U.S. Ohio Replacement and UK Successor common missile compartment program development
proposals.rationale: The announcement uses both 'Ohio Replacement' and 'common missile compartment' - the PE title and the exact lexicon name that PE 0603595N owns - and describes the scope as 'program development', which is the development appropriation this RDT&E PE funds. Missile fire control for the US/UK common missile compartment is the CMC program's own design work, not sustainment of a fielded platform, and no other PE in this index carries the CMC name. This is a separable scope line within a multi-part Strategic Systems Programs contract, so the proposal claims only that portion of the action.

refute_a.reason: Development work against a development line: the announcement's scope for this leg is 'the missile fire control for the U.S. Ohio Replacement and UK Successor common missile compartment program development', and the lake records 017-1319 (RDT&E, Navy) among this PIID's funding accounts, matching PE 0603595N's account 1319N; the CMC is the program's own design work that this PE funds, not a fielded platform being sustained, and 'Ohio Replacement' is a single named development program rather than a catch-all.

refute_b.reason: 'Common Missile Compartment (CMC)' is owned by 0603595N alone; the nearest alternative, SCN line 1045 'COLUMBIA Class Submarine', owns 'Missile Tube Module (MTM)' and hull numbers but not the CMC name, and the announcement's own words ('common missile compartment program development', 'Ohio Replacement' - the PE's title) point at the development PE rather than the construction line, so no competing owner in this index takes the same evidence.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Ship self-defense system design and production
proposals.rationale: The announcement's 'Ship self-defense system' differs from the index name 'Ships Self Defense System (SSDS)' only by a plural and a hyphen, so it is the same system under an alias rather than a generic English phrase. The award covers design AND production of SSDS, administered by NSWC Dahlgren - the SSDS technical agent - which is the end item the OPN line 5231 'Ship Missile Support Equipment' buys in its own narrative. No other row in this index owns the SSDS name, and the action is production, not base operations or a facility service.

refute_a.reason: Money colour is disjoint and unverifiable: BLI 5231 carries account 1810N (017-1810, OPN) but the only funding account the lake records for N0017816D3001 is 017-1319 (RDT&E, Navy), and the announcement itself obligates no funds at award ('funds will be obligated on individual orders'), names no appropriation, and covers 'design and production' together - an IDIQ ceiling action whose work cannot be shown to belong to this procurement line's appropriation.

refute_b.reason: The announcement never writes 'SSDS' nor any Mk designator - only the lowercase descriptive phrase 'Ship self-defense system' in a one-line IDIQ modification with no funds obligated - so it reads as the generic capability category (§3's weak-generic-name reject) rather than the proper name 5231 owns, and this index publishes several distinct ship self-defense systems under other lines (4205 'Phalanx Close-In Weapon System (CIWS)', 2242 'Rolling Airframe Missile (RAM)', 2307 'Evolved Sea Sparrow Missile (ESSM)') that the same phrase would cover equally well; the alias is not established.

proposals.announcement_evidence: in support of the Aircraft Launch and Recovery Equipment Information Systems Program
proposals.rationale: The index name 'Aircraft Launch and Recovery Equipment (ALRE)' appears verbatim inside the announcement's program title, and BLI 4213 'Aircraft Support Equipment' is the OPN line whose narrative owns ALRE. The action procures up to 60 Moriah wind systems plus sub-components and repair services - shipboard launch-and-recovery hardware, the line's own end item - and the announcement names fiscal 2015 other procurement (Navy) funds, so the money colour matches a procurement line. The RDT&E owner of a similar name (0604512N 'ALRE Modernization') is not proposed because this is a production buy, not development.

refute_a.reason: The announcement names fiscal 2015 other procurement (Navy) funds, which is exactly BLI 4213's account 1810N, and the core scope is procuring up to 60 Moriah wind systems with their sub-components - shipboard launch-and-recovery hardware that is the Aircraft Support Equipment line's own end item, not a platform the contract merely supports; 'Aircraft Support Equipment' is a named procurement line, not a CATCHALL_TITLE aggregate.

refute_b.reason: Two rows own an ALRE name - 4213 'Aircraft Launch and Recovery Equipment (ALRE)' and 0604512N 'Aircraft Launch & Recovery Equipment (ALRE) Modernization' - and neither owns the program the announcement actually names, the 'Aircraft Launch and Recovery Equipment INFORMATION SYSTEMS Program' (ALRE-IS), nor the Moriah wind system being bought; the link rests on the ALRE string being contained inside a longer, differently-named sub-program, which is a different increment from the lexicon name.

proposals.announcement_evidence: accomplishment of a post shakedown availability for a littoral combat ship
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the littoral combat ship exactly as the SCN line 2127 'Littoral Combat Ship' carries it, and the work is a post shakedown availability - the post-delivery work the shipbuilding line itself funds as part of delivering the ship. proposals.announcement_evidence: procurement of 7,365 Enhanced Laser Guided Training Round (ELGTR) BDU-59B/B units
proposals.rationale: The ELGTR is the enhanced variant of the Laser Guided Training Round the Practice Bombs line 0160 owns in its narrative, so the designator differs only by the 'Enhanced' variant prefix. proposals.rationale: 'DDG 51' and the index name 'DDG-51' differ only by the hyphen in the designator. Follow yard support is the shipbuilder engineering service the SCN destroyer line itself funds for the hulls it is building, and the announcement confirms fiscal 2017-2020 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds - the exact appropriation of BLI 2122. The ship class here is the program the line funds, not a platform that some other system is being bought for.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the U.S. SSGN Attack Weapon Control System, including training and support equipment and research and development
proposals.rationale: The announcement carries the index name 'Attack Weapon Control System' verbatim, and BLI 5420 'SSN Combat Control Systems' is the only line in this index that owns it. proposals.program_name: The F/A-18 and EA-18G Service Life Assessment Program (SLAP)
proposals.announcement_evidence: continued support of the F/A-18E/F and EA-18G Service Life Assessment Program and Service Life Extension Program
proposals.lexicon_quote: The F/A-18 and EA-18G Service Life Assessment Program (SLAP)
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the F/A-18E/F and EA-18G Service Life Assessment Program, which is the same program the PE 0702207N narrative owns as 'The F/A-18 and EA-18G Service Life Assessment Program (SLAP)' - only the E/F variant suffix differs. refute_a.reason: The scope - fatigue-life assessment of the structure, change proposals, and planning the physical modification for life extension - is analytical depot-maintenance engineering, which is precisely what RDT&E PE 0702207N (account 1319N) exists to fund, not O&M depot execution; the lake records no funding accounts for this PIID so nothing contradicts that colour, and the named thing is the SLAP/SLEP the PE's own narrative owns, with the F/A-18E/F and EA-18G being the subject of the assessment rather than a platform an unrelated buy supports.

refute_b.reason: Both names the announcement uses - Service Life Assessment Program and Service Life Extension Program - sit on the same PE (0702207N owns 'The F/A-18 and EA-18G Service Life Assessment Program (SLAP)' and 'Service Life Extension Program (SLEP)'), and the competing life-extension rows belong to other platforms (0530 MH-60S SLEP, 3141 MK-30 SLEP, 5139 LCAC SLEP) or to a differently named program the announcement never mentions (0525 'OSIP 14-26 Service Life Modification (SLM)'); 'F/A-18E/F' is a subset of the lexicon name's 'F/A-18', not a rival increment.

proposals.rationale: The award buys LRIP Lot 9 air-vehicle initial spares including F-35B aloft spares packages for the Marine Corps, and F-35B maps to the JSF STOVL line 0152 by variant. But spares packages are budgeted as a separate spares element rather than as the aircraft line's own end item, the announcement text visible here never states which appropriation or BLI is obligated, and the index carries the JSF name on two lines (0147 CV and 0152 STOVL) plus several F-35 RDT&E PEs. The evidence does not establish that this money is the STOVL procurement line's own work, so it does not meet the standard for a published high-tier attribution.

'Next Generation Enterprise Network' appears verbatim in the announcement and exactly matches the name PE 0605013N 'Information Technology Development' owns. But the buy is 22,001 commodity laptops funded with fiscal 2013/2014 procurement (Marine Corps) money on a MARCORSYSCOM requirements contract, which is neither the Navy RDT&E appropriation of 0605013N nor the Navy OPN line 8164 that owns 'The Next Generation Network (NGEN)'. A hardware refresh bought with PMC dollars is not the IT-development PE's own work, and the name collides across at least two index owners, so the attribution cannot be published.

The E-2 name the announcement carries is owned by the APN mods line 0544 'E-2 Series' (and by several E-2D PEs), but the option exercised here provides sustainment and technical support for the governments of France, Japan, Taiwan and Egypt, paid with Foreign Military Sales customer funds. FMS customer money does not pay for the US line's own work, and sustainment support is the O&M-flavoured failure mode the rubric warns about when it is attached to a US procurement line. The bare designator 'E-2' is also one of the most heavily collided names in this index.

The announcement names the Evolved SeaSparrow Missile, which the WPN line 2307 'ESSM' owns (spelling of 'Sea Sparrow' aside), so the identity is real. But the action exercises options for engineering and technical support across the ESSM and NATO SeaSparrow Missile Systems programs and states the obligation as fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023 'other customer funds', not weapons procurement - a consortium/other-customer colour that does not establish the WPN line's own buy. The same ESSM name is also owned by 6120 'Spares and Repair Parts' in this index, leaving the owner unresolved.

proposals.program_name: Mode 5 Systems Engineering and Integrated Logistics Support (ILS)
proposals.rationale: 'Mode 5' is a name PE 0604777N 'Navigation/ID System' owns, and the option procures APX-111(V) Mode 5 combined interrogator transponders and upgrade kits. But 0604777N is an RDT&E development PE whose Mode 5 rows describe systems engineering and ILS for the AN/UPX-29 and UPX-36, while this is a hardware production option partly funded by Finland and Switzerland under FMS; the APX-111 designator appears nowhere in this index, and the OPN 'ID Systems' line 2851 carries only AN/APX-123 and the Mark XII/XIIA system. Neither candidate is established as the owner of this buy.

proposals.program_name: Mode 5 Systems Engineering and Integrated Logistics Support (ILS)
proposals.rationale: Same contract family as record 31 and the same problem: the announcement's 'Mode 5 combined interrogator transponder kits' and APX-111 Identification Friend or Foe units touch the Mode 5 name that RDT&E PE 0604777N owns, but this is a production option for hardware and repair articles co-funded by Finland and Switzerland through FMS, not the development and ILS effort the PE narrative describes. The APX-111 designator is absent from this org's index, so no line is shown to own the item being bought.

proposals.program_name: GERALD R FORD CI NUC AIRCRAFT CARRIER CVN 78-80
proposals.rationale: 'Ford Class' aliases the CVN 78-80 name PE 0604112N owns, but the award buys shore-based spares - switchboards and load centers - with fiscal 2023 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds, and 0604112N is an RDT&E development PE. The announcement names Northrop F-5F and F-5N aircraft, and 'F-5' is a name the APN line 0522 'Adversary' owns. A bare two-character type designator is also weak identity evidence on its own.

The award covers design, development, testing and production of submarine photonics masts, but the announcement names no specific mast - it never says Low Profile Photonics Mast or Photonics Mast Variant - and the index carries the LPPM name under three different owners (0604503N, 0604777N and 0840). The obligation is overwhelmingly fiscal 2020 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) money, which is not the OPN colour of 0840 'Sub Periscope, Imaging and Supt Equip Prog'. Generic 'photonics masts' is not enough to pick one owner.

The announcement names the Air and Missile Defense Radar (AMDR) program, which is the title of PE 0604522N, and AN/SPY-6 is the radar AMDR became - so the identity is real but indirect, since the announcement never uses the AN/SPY-6 designator that is the actual index name. The option buys systems engineering, ship integration and land-based test-site support funded with fiscal 2016 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) money, a ship-construction appropriation rather than the RDT&E colour of this PE. Ship-integration engineering paid from SCN is exactly the money-colour failure mode the rubric flags.
